prompt: The value of A·(A × B) is:
explain: A × B is perpendicular to A, so the dot product is zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which of these physical quantities is a cross product of two vectors?
explain: L = r × p; power and work are dot products, KE is a scalar.

subject: Physics
prompt: The torque on an electric dipole, τ = p × E, vanishes when the angle between p and E is:
explain: τ = pE sinθ = 0 for θ = 0° or 180°.

subject: Physics
prompt: The magnitude |A × B| represents geometrically the:

subject: Physics
prompt: Which of these is NOT a dot product of two vectors?
explain: Torque = r × F is a cross product; W = F·s, P = F·v, φ = B·A are dot products.

subject: Physics
prompt: Ball A is thrown up at speed u from ground; ball B is dropped from height h at the same instant. They meet after:
explain: Relative acceleration is zero; relative speed is u, so t = h/u.

subject: Physics
prompt: If v_AB = 0 for two bodies on a line, their separation:
explain: Equal velocities mean no relative motion, so the gap stays constant.

subject: Physics
prompt: On velocity–time graphs of two bodies, the intersection point means:
options: They have the same velocity then
explain: v–t crossing means v_A = v_B (v_rel = 0), not necessarily the same position.

subject: Physics
prompt: From one point, one ball is thrown up and another down, both at speed u. Their relative velocity in flight:
explain: Both have acceleration g, so v_rel stays at u − (−u) = 2u.

subject: Physics
prompt: A car starts from rest with uniform acceleration behind a truck moving at constant speed. Separation is extreme when:
options: The car's velocity is double the truck's
explain: Separation is stationary (d(Δx)/dt = 0) when the relative velocity is zero, i.e. the velocities are equal.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two frames move with constant relative velocity. A body's accelerations measured in them are:
options: Differ by the relative speed ÷ time
explain: The relative acceleration of the frames is zero, so a' = a. This is Galilean invariance of acceleration.

subject: Physics
topic: Projectile: range, max height, time of flight
prompt: Same speed, angles α and (90° − α). Ratio of times of flight T₁/T₂ is:
explain: T ∝ sinα, and sinα/sin(90°−α) = sinα/cosα = tanα.

subject: Physics
topic: Projectile: range, max height, time of flight
prompt: A projectile of mass m is launched at α with speed u and lands at the same level. Change in momentum is:
explain: Horizontal momentum is unchanged; vertical goes from +mu sinα to −mu sinα, so Δp = 2mu sinα downward.

subject: Physics
prompt: Speed v, angular displacement θ in uniform circular motion. Magnitude of change in velocity is
explain: Chord of the velocity-vector triangle gives |Δv| = 2v sin(θ/2).

subject: Physics
prompt: For a particle in uniform circular motion, the average velocity over one full revolution is
explain: Net displacement over a full revolution is zero, so average velocity is zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: At constant speed, the graph of centripetal acceleration versus radius r is a
explain: a ∝ 1/r at constant v gives a rectangular hyperbola.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two particles move in circles of radii r₁ and r₂ with equal periods. Ratio of centripetal accelerations a₁/a₂ is
explain: With equal T, a = 4π²r/T² ∝ r, so a₁/a₂ = r₁/r₂.

subject: Physics
prompt: Dot product A·B is commutative, while the cross product A × B is:
explain: A × B = −B × A, direction reverses on swapping order.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done W = F·s is a:
explain: Dot product of two vectors gives a scalar.

subject: Physics
prompt: Power P = F·v is a scalar, because it is a:
explain: Dot product of force and velocity gives a scalar.

subject: Physics
prompt: For A·B = AB (maximum positive value), the angle between A and B is:
explain: A·B = AB cosθ is maximum at θ = 0°.

subject: Physics
prompt: For three nonzero vectors, A·(B × C) = 0 means the vectors are:
explain: Zero parallelepiped volume means the three vectors lie in one plane.

subject: Physics
prompt: The scalar triple product A·(B × C) equals:
explain: Cyclic permutation (A,B,C)→(C,A,B) keeps the sign; swapping two vectors reverses it.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which pair of unit-vector products is correct?
explain: Cyclic order î→ĵ→k̂ gives positive results: ĵ × k̂ = î; î × k̂ = −ĵ and k̂ × î = ĵ.

subject: Physics
topic: Projectile: range, max height, time of flight
prompt: Projectile launched at 60° to horizontal. KE at highest point as fraction of initial KE:
explain: Only horizontal component survives: cos²60° = 1/4.

subject: Physics
topic: Projectile: range, max height, time of flight
prompt: Two projectiles fired together from one point. Motion of one as seen from the other is:
options: A straight line only if same speed
explain: Relative acceleration is zero, so relative velocity is constant: straight-line path.

subject: Physics
topic: Projectile: range, max height, time of flight
prompt: Range of a projectile launched at 15° with speed u on level ground:
explain: sin30° = 1/2, so R = u²/2g.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two cars approach each other head-on at constant speeds. Their separation vs time graph is:
explain: Relative velocity is constant and closing, so separation decreases linearly until they meet.

subject: Physics
prompt: A car's speedometer reading at any instant gives its:
explain: A speedometer shows the magnitude only, with no direction, at that instant: instantaneous speed.

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle has v = −5 m/s and a = −2 m/s² along a line. Its speed is:
options: Increasing, since a and v have same sign
explain: When a and v point the same way (both negative here), speed increases. Sign of a alone does not decide.

subject: Physics
prompt: A car covers three equal distances at v₁, v₂, v₃. Its average speed is:
explain: Equal distances give the harmonic mean: total distance/total time = 3/(1/v₁ + 1/v₂ + 1/v₃).

subject: Physics
prompt: In straight-line motion, at the instant speed is maximum (smooth variation), acceleration is:
explain: Speed is at an extremum, so dv/dt = 0 and the acceleration is zero at that instant.

subject: Physics
prompt: The direction of the average velocity vector over an interval is along the:
explain: v_avg = Δr/Δt, a positive scalar multiple of the displacement, so it points along the displacement.

subject: Physics
prompt: A ball thrown up at speed u passes a height h at times t₁ (up) and t₂ (down). t₁ + t₂ =
explain: Sum of roots of ½gt² − ut + h = 0 is 2u/g.

subject: Physics
prompt: Speed–time graph of a ball thrown up and caught back at the start (no air drag) is:
options: V-shape, vertex on the axis at the top
explain: Speed = |v|. It falls linearly to zero at the top, then rises linearly. Both slopes have magnitude g.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two vectors of equal magnitude A are inclined at angle θ. Their resultant has magnitude:
explain: R² = 2A²(1 + cosθ) = 4A²cos²(θ/2), so R = 2A cos(θ/2).

subject: Physics
prompt: As the angle between two vectors of fixed magnitudes rises from 0° to 180°, the resultant's magnitude:
explain: R² = A² + B² + 2AB cosθ and cosθ decreases on 0° to 180°, so R falls from A+B to |A−B|.

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle revolves at 120 revolutions per minute. Its angular velocity is:
explain: n = 2 rev/s, so ω = 2π × 2 = 4π rad/s.
